result.topic_en: Latin notes on the Paris prize problem on heat conduction, classifying the forms a solution u of $\Delta u=0$, $\Lambda u=\partial u/\partial t$ can take, depending on how many equations the condition F=0 splits into (cases m=3 and m=4).
result.transcription:
denotantibus a, b, c functiones solarum $\beta$ & $t$, p & q autem functiones solarum $\alpha$ & $\beta$. Jam in locum ipsius
$\alpha$ [-nova-] variabilis independens q introduci potest. Quo pacto [-erit-] obtinetur
$u = ap + \alpha b + c$. [-ubi-] [-quae-] [-in qua expressione-] {+ubi+} jam sola p est functio ambarum variabilium {+$\alpha$ & $\beta$+}
Substituendo hanc [-valorem-] expressionem in aequationibus
$\Delta u = 0 \quad \Lambda u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$ {+coefficientium formae facile eruuntur.+}
[-coef-] [-coefficientes harum aequationum facile per functionem p exprimuntur-]. Sed hoc hic non persequemur,
quum hic casus in corporibus homogeneis occurrere nequeat.
Restat casus, quando jam una aequationum, in quas aequatio F=0 discinditur, formam (1) habet ideoque
[-quum e-] formam
$r\frac{\partial u}{\partial \alpha} + s\frac{\partial u}{\partial \beta} = 0.$
[-Tum u-] Tum [-erit-] u erit [-formae-]
$u = ap + b$
denotantibus a & b functiones {+solarum+} [-ipsarum-] $\beta$ & $t$ et p functionem solarum $\alpha$ & $\beta$, [-vel-] Si in locum ipsius $\alpha$ varia
bilis independens p introducitur, [-erit-] prodibit
[-$u = \alpha + b$-] $\frac{\partial u}{\partial \alpha} = 0$
et aequatio abit in $\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial \alpha^2} = 0$.

Invenimus igitur, si m=2 sive aequatio F=0 in duas aequationes
$\Delta u = 0$
$\Lambda u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$
dissolvatur, esse aut $[-\Delta\Lambda-] = [-\Theta\Delta-]$ aut functionem u compositam esse a numero finito terminorum formae
$f(t)\, e^{\lambda t}$, in quibus $\lambda$ constans & $f(t)$ functio integra ipsius t est.

[-quadratum aut-]
aut formam induere [-$ap + b +$-] $\varphi(\beta,t)\,\chi(\alpha,\beta) + \alpha\,\varphi_1(\beta,t) + \varphi_2(\beta,t)$

Si m=3 functionem aut {+esse+} e numero finito terminorum formae $f(t)\, e^{\lambda t}$ [-constantem-]
aut [-ein-] formae $\varphi(\beta,t)\,\alpha + \varphi_1(\beta,t)$
[-Aut-] Denique m=4 nullo negotio penitus absolvi potest.
Si enim praeter aequationem $\Lambda u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$ habentur tres aequationes [-inter-] inter $\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial \alpha^2}, \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial \alpha \partial \beta}, \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial \beta^2}, \frac{\partial u}{\partial \alpha}, \frac{\partial u}{\partial \beta}$,
aut prodibit aequatio formae $r\frac{\partial u}{\partial \alpha} + s\frac{\partial u}{\partial \beta}$ {+$=0$+}[?] et proin variabiles independentes ita eligere licet, ut u fiat
functio unius tantum variabilis, aut [-$\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial \alpha^2}, \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial \alpha\partial\beta}, \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\beta^2}$-] [-per $\frac{\partial u}{\partial \alpha}, \frac{\partial u}{\partial \beta}$ exprimi possunt-]
ideoque etiam $\Lambda u, \Lambda^2 u, \Lambda^3 u$ per $\frac{\partial u}{\partial \alpha}, \frac{\partial u}{\partial \beta}$ exprimi possunt. Tum autem [-obtineri potest-] {+emerget+} aequatio
formae
$[-a\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial t^3}-] \; a\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial t^3} + b\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} + c\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = 0$
[-unde-] u [-erit formae-] {+habebit formam+}
$p\,e^{\lambda t} + q\,e^{\mu t} + r$ vel $(p\, [-e^{\lambda t} +-] + q t)\, e^{\lambda t} + r$
patetque per praecedentia, $\lambda$ & $\mu$ esse constantes.
Jam sumto p pro variabili independente $\alpha$ et substitutis his {+expressionibus+} [-valoribus-] in aequatione $\Lambda u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$
invenitur fieri non posse, ut q sit functio ipsius $\alpha$, [-nisi quum-] {+nisi+} $\lambda$ & $\mu$ sint [-diversae-] inaequales {+&+}
Ergo p & q [-locum-] {+vice+} variabilium independentium fungi possunt. Praeterea [-invenitur-] ex aequatione
$\Lambda u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$ {+invenitur+} $r$ = const.
In hoc igitur casu u aut est functio unius tantum variabilis {+ipsius t+}[?] [-$f + \alpha$-]
aut [-formae-] alterutram {+utram+}[?] formarum
$\alpha e^{\lambda t} + \beta e^{\mu t}$ + const. $(\alpha + \beta t)\, e^{\lambda t}$ + const.
induit, valore $\mu = 0$ non excluso.

methods.what: Change of independent variable so u becomes linear in a new variable
First-order condition implies u linear in function p; after change of variable second derivative vanishes
Case m=2: u is finite sum of quasi-polynomial exponentials or of given separated form
methods.quote: $f(t)\, e^{\lambda t}$, in quibus $\lambda$ constans & $f(t)$ functio integra ipsius t est.

methods.what: Case m=4: third-order constant-coefficient ODE in t leads to exponential solutions
methods.quote: $a\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial t^3} + b\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} + c\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = 0$
$\alpha e^{\lambda t} + \beta e^{\mu t}$ + const. $(\alpha + \beta t)\, e^{\lambda t}$ + const.

items.quote:
Sed hoc hic non persequemur,
quum hic casus in corporibus homogeneis occurrere nequeat.
items.english: But we will not pursue this here, since this case cannot occur in homogeneous bodies.

items.quote: Denique m=4 nullo negotio penitus absolvi potest.
items.english: Finally m=4 can be completely settled without any trouble.

items.quote: invenitur fieri non posse, ut q sit functio ipsius $\alpha$, [-nisi quum-] {+nisi+} $\lambda$ & $\mu$ sint [-diversae-] inaequales
items.english: It is found that it is impossible for q to be a function of alpha unless lambda and mu are unequal.

items.quote:
Praeterea [-invenitur-] ex aequatione
$\Lambda u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$ {+invenitur+} $r$ = const.
items.english: Moreover from the equation Lambda u = du/dt one finds r = const.
